This comparison analyzes the median time to CT scanning, measured in minutes, across national, regional, and hospital levels in Denmark. The data provides a comprehensive breakdown of patient wait times, including the first quartile (Q1), median, and third quartile (Q3) for each facility and region. Because the evidence is drawn from a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends can be established; however, the snapshot reveals significant disparities in imaging efficiency across the Danish healthcare system.

At the national level, the overall median time to a CT scan in [[danmark|Danmark]] is 174 minutes, with a Q3 of 348 minutes [^src1]. When examining regional aggregates, [[midtjylland-region-i-alt|Midtjylland Region i alt]] demonstrates the fastest regional median at 131 minutes, while [[hovedstaden-region-i-alt|Hovedstaden Region i alt]] and [[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland Region i alt]] report slower medians of 182 and 192 minutes, respectively [^src1]. 

The most striking outlier in the dataset is [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]], which records a median wait time of 589 minutes [^src1]. More alarmingly, its third quartile (Q3) reaches an extreme 3,962 minutes, vastly exceeding the national Q3 and indicating that a quarter of its patients experience exceptionally prolonged delays before receiving a CT scan [^src1]. Other hospitals with notably high median wait times include [[amager-og-hvidovre-hospital|Amager og Hvidovre Hospital]] at 262 minutes, [[naestved-slagese-og-ringsted-sygehuse|Næstved, Slagelse og Ringsted sygehuse]] at 252 minutes, and [[aalborg-universitetshospital|Aalborg Universitetshospital]] at 246 minutes [^src1].

Conversely, several hospitals perform significantly better than the national median. [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] leads the dataset with the lowest median time of just 87 minutes, alongside a tight interquartile range (Q1: 52, Q3: 133) [^src1]. [[regionshospitalet-randers|Regionshospitalet Randers]] follows with a median of 114 minutes, and [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]] records a median of 119 minutes [^src1]. [[regionshospitalet-goedstrup|Regionshospitalet Gødstrup]] also performs well, with a median of 126 minutes [^src1]. These facilities demonstrate that rapid CT scanning is achievable within the public hospital system, contrasting sharply with the severe bottlenecks observed at larger university hospitals like Rigshospitalet.

While this analysis focuses on the 2025 data for CT scanning times, the broader AKDB annual reports from 2023, 2024, and 2025 provide extensive additional context on other acute surgical metrics, demographic variables, and historical trends across the Danish healthcare system [^src2] [^src3] [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11] [^src12] [^src13] [^src14] [^src15] [^src16] [^src17] [^src18] [^src19] [^src20] [^src21] [^src22].
